---
title: "Warping"
description: "gdalxarray.warp() builds a warped-VRT recipe; xarray opens it lazily."
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
from _common import *
import sys
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm

sys.path.insert(0, str(DOCS.parent / "scripts" / "fixtures"))
from make_warp import warp_direct  # the settings the pinned oracle was made with

man = data_json("warp/manifest.json")
seaice = data(next(c["source"] for c in man["cases"] if c["source"].startswith("seaice/")))
gebco = data(next(c["source"] for c in man["cases"] if c["source"].startswith("gebco/")))
```

`gdalxarray.warp()` wraps `gdal.Warp(..., format="VRT")` and returns
the VRT as a string. Nothing is resampled until values are read, and
then only for the cells asked for. The recipe is a few kilobytes
whatever the size of the source.

## Antarctic sea ice to longitude and latitude

One day of Antarctic sea-ice concentration from passive microwave, on
the grid it is published on: 25 km polar stereographic cells on the
Hughes 1980 ellipsoid (EPSG:3412, not the WGS84-based EPSG:3031).
Land, coast and the pole hole are nodata.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
provenance("seaice")
```

```{python}
src = xr.open_dataset(seaice, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
src["band_data"].shape, src.xindexes["crs"].crs.to_epsg()
```

```{python}
recipe = gdalxarray.warp(seaice, crs="EPSG:4326", bbox=(-180, -90, 180, -50),
                         resolution=(0.25, 0.125), resampling="bilinear")
print(f"{len(recipe)} characters of VRT")
print("\n".join(recipe.splitlines()[:6]))
```

The recipe opens like any other source, in classic mode:

```{python}
ll = xr.open_dataset(recipe, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
ll["band_data"]
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Sea-ice concentration near the winter maximum: as stored on the NSIDC polar stereographic grid (left), and warped to longitude/latitude south of 50S on read (right). Grey is land, coast and the pole hole."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.6), layout="constrained",
                        gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1, 1.7]))
kw = dict(cmap="Blues_r", vmin=0, vmax=1)
src["band_data"].isel(band=0).plot(ax=axs[0], add_colorbar=False, **kw)
axs[0].set_aspect("equal"); axs[0].set_title("EPSG:3412, as stored")
ll["band_data"].isel(band=0).plot(ax=axs[1], cbar_kwargs={"label": "concentration"}, **kw)
axs[1].set_title("EPSG:4326, warped on read")
for ax in axs:
    ax.set_facecolor("0.7")
plt.show()
```

## Any target the warper can express

Target CRS, extent and size are all recipe parameters. Global
bathymetry and topography, averaged to half a degree, in three
projections, the last centred on Hobart:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
provenance("gebco")
```

```{python}
targets = {
    "Antarctic polar stereographic": dict(crs="EPSG:3031", bbox=(-4e6, -4e6, 4e6, 4e6), shape=(320, 320)),
    "Equal Earth": dict(crs="+proj=eqearth", bbox=(-17.3e6, -8.4e6, 17.3e6, 8.4e6), shape=(500, 243)),
    "Orthographic over Hobart": dict(crs="+proj=ortho +lat_0=-42.9 +lon_0=147.3",
                                     bbox=(-6.4e6, -6.4e6, 6.4e6, 6.4e6), shape=(320, 320)),
}
# nodata marks cells outside a projection's domain (GEBCO itself has none)
warped = {k: xr.open_dataset(gdalxarray.warp(gebco, resampling="bilinear", nodata=-32768, **t),
                             engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)["band_data"].isel(band=0)
          for k, t in targets.items()}
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "GEBCO elevation (metres) through three warped VRT recipes: polar stereographic, Equal Earth, and an orthographic view centred on Hobart."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 4.2), layout="constrained",
                        gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1, 1.8, 1]))
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-7000, vcenter=0, vmax=4000)
for ax, (name, da) in zip(axs, warped.items()):
    im = ax.imshow(np.ma.masked_invalid(da.values), cmap="gist_earth", norm=norm)
    ax.set_title(name); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
fig.colorbar(im, ax=axs, shrink=0.8, label="elevation (m)")
plt.show()
```

Extra keywords go straight to `gdal.WarpOptions`, so cutlines,
transformer options, geolocation arrays, working type and so on are
available. [Curvilinear grids](curvilinear.qmd) uses `geoloc=True`.

## Checked against GDAL

`scripts/fixtures/make_warp.py` defines target grids over these two
sources (lon/lat, WGS84 polar stereographic, Equal Earth, orthographic,
and two coarse cases where GDAL reads an overview) and records what
`gdal.Warp` writes for each: into memory, single-threaded, error
threshold 0.125. For each case this page compares:

- **gdalxarray**: `gdalxarray.warp()` opened with xarray;
- **GDAL VRT**: the same warped VRT read by GDAL itself
  (`gdal.Warp(format="VRT")` then `ReadAsArray`);
- **GDAL direct**: `gdal.Warp` into memory with the same settings as the
  recorded case, using the GDAL this page was built with;
- **pinned**: the recorded result, from the GDAL version in the
  manifest.

gdalxarray must agree with the GDAL VRT on every cell: that is the
claim this package makes, that it adds nothing to what GDAL reads. The
other two columns are reported, not required. A warped VRT computes
each block on its own, so where the approximate transformer struggles
(near a pole, say) it can differ from a single direct warp; and GDAL's
resampling kernels can change between releases.

```{python}
def same(a, b):
    return float(np.mean((a == b) | (np.isnan(a) & np.isnan(b)))) if a.dtype.kind == "f" \
        else float(np.mean(a == b))


rows = []
for c in man["cases"]:
    gt, W, H = c["geotransform"], c["width"], c["height"]
    bbox = (gt[0], gt[3] + gt[5] * H, gt[0] + gt[1] * W, gt[3])
    pinned_all = np.load(data("warp/" + c["file"]))
    for m in c["resampling"]:
        kw = dict(crs=c["crs"], bbox=bbox, shape=(W, H), resampling=m,
                  errorThreshold=c["error_threshold"])
        if c["overview"] == "none":
            kw["overviewLevel"] = "NONE"
        vrt = gdalxarray.warp(data(c["source"]), **kw)
        gx = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False,
                             mask_and_scale=False)["band_data"].values[0]
        vrt_gdal = gdal.Open(vrt).ReadAsArray()
        direct = warp_direct(data(c["source"]), c["crs"], gt, W, H, m, c["overview"])
        rows.append({"case": c["name"], "resampling": m,
                     "gdalxarray = GDAL VRT": same(gx, vrt_gdal),
                     "GDAL VRT = GDAL direct": same(vrt_gdal, direct),
                     "GDAL direct = pinned": same(direct, pinned_all[m])})

tab = pd.DataFrame(rows)
tab.style.format("{:.2%}", subset=tab.columns[2:]).hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
bad = tab[tab["gdalxarray = GDAL VRT"] < 1]
print(f"Pinned oracle from GDAL {man['gdal']}; this page built with GDAL {gdal.__version__}. "
      f"gdalxarray matches GDAL's own read of the VRT in {len(tab) - len(bad)} of {len(tab)} cases; "
      f"{(tab['GDAL direct = pinned'] == 1).sum()} of {len(tab)} direct warps match the pinned oracle exactly.")
print()
assert bad.empty, bad
```
